## Traps

Each of these cost at least one lost or mis-published change. Most are hook-enforced or fixed in the tools above; the
rest are discipline.

| trap | what happens | do instead |
|---|---|---|
| `git add a b c 2>/dev/null` | one missing path fails the WHOLE add silently; the commit then runs on an empty or partial index and "succeeds" | never silence `git add`; check `git show --stat HEAD` |
| a deleted path on `git add` | `git add <deleted>` errors and kills the `&&` chain; the push after it says "Everything up-to-date" | put a deleted path on the commit pathspec only |
| pathspec commit takes the WORKTREE | `git commit <path>` is an implicit `git add` of that path: a blob you staged with `update-index` is ignored, and a peer's unsaved lines in the same file ride along | check `git diff --stat <path>` first; build partial commits in a temp index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`) |
| pathspec commit cannot remove-but-keep | `git rm --cached p` then `git commit p` re-adds `p` from the worktree | commit through a temp index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=… git read-tree HEAD; git rm --cached …; write-tree; commit-tree`), then `git reset -q -- p` in the real index |
| untracked can't be pathspec-committed | `git commit <new file>` → "did not match any file(s) known to git"; a `git commit <dir>` silently skips new files in it | `git add -- <new file>` first (explicit path), then `git commit <paths>` |
| `-F -` after `--` | `git commit -- p -F -` treats `-F` and `-` as pathspecs | options before `--`, paths after |
| bare `git commit` | commits the WHOLE index, including what a helper staged in the same clone | always name paths (hook-enforced) |
| `.git/index.lock` exists | a background helper's read-only `git status` holds it for a second; a failed `./publish` then committed NONE of its paths | wait a few seconds and retry; never delete a lock younger than a minute; check `git status` after any failed publish |
| compound command refused whole | a `PreToolUse` hook (blanket stage, DLL stamp, sheet guard) refuses the entire Bash call before the shell runs — any file write chained before the commit never happened either | keep file writes and git commands in SEPARATE Bash calls; a hook's refusal means nothing in that call ran |
| zsh refspec modifier | `git push origin $N:refs/heads/main` — zsh reads `:r` as a modifier and mangles the refspec | `"${N}:refs/heads/main"` |
| land.sh duplicates | landing by plumbing leaves the clone "ahead N, behind M" with patch-equivalent copies; a stale clone shows phantom selftest reds (ledger_lint NOT_APPEND, a "lost" bridge tool) | `land.sh` now syncs itself; otherwise `./sync`. Re-check a red on a synced clone before fixing it |
| autostash | `pull --rebase --autostash` re-applied peers' dirty files and stranded 53 in `stash@{0}` (2026-10-10) | never stash; `./publish` and `./sync` use `reset --keep` |
| pre-push ledger lint judges the LOCAL HEAD | a correct plumbing push from a clone behind origin is refused NOT_APPEND | `./sync` first, then land |
| served review-sheet output | all of `Transient/` is untracked since 2026-10-18 except `*.decisions.json` and pins; `refresh_sheets.py` prints `UNPUBLISHED:` only for a rebuilt sheet that is pinned (tracked) | publish a pinned rebuilt sheet; an unpinned one needs nothing |
| a fetch OOM-kills the window | fetching the 5.5 GiB pack inside a 10G-capped seat scope | `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet -p MemoryMax=20G git fetch origin main` |
| a real merge commit | the blanket-stage hook refuses `git commit --no-edit` mid-merge (no pathspec possible) | `GIT_EDITOR=true git merge --continue` |
| `handoff.py` UNPUSHED gate refuses a fully published tree | the gate compares SHAs, not patches; publish rebases, so the local SHAs differ from origin's | prove equivalence with `git log --cherry-mark origin/main...HEAD`, then `./sync`; do not reach for `--force` |
| `handoff.py --wake` in a stale shared checkout | it prints that checkout's newest handoff, not origin's, so a window can wake on an old one | read `git show origin/main:infrastructure/state/handoffs/<newest>` instead |
| a plumbing-built push (patch diffed from the wrong parent, `git apply` failing inside a pipe to `tail`) | pushed an EMPTY commit with a misleading message | assert the apply succeeded (`set -o pipefail`) and that the resulting tree differs from `origin/main` before pushing |
| `git commit && git pull --rebase && git push` in ONE Bash call | the pre-push/PreToolUse ledger hook judges HEAD BEFORE the compound runs, so it is refused NOT_APPEND even though the rebase would fix it | run commit, pull/rebase and push as separate Bash calls; never stash a peer's dirty files to rebase (`./publish` replays without a stash) |
| `./publish` refuses ('not mine to overwrite', `reset --keep` refused, exit 2) because a PEER has an uncommitted edit to a file origin changed, or to the mod DLL pair (their `winbuild.py` output, `+dirty` in the `.srchash`) | your commit stays local and every later publish waits on that peer; the temp-index + `commit-tree` + push workaround is refused by the ledger_lint push hook, which lints the stale local HEAD | land WITHOUT touching the tree: `tree=$(git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=C^ origin/main C)`; `commit-tree` it onto `origin/main`; `git push origin <tip>:main` (local main stays diverged; the next publish's `git cherry` skips it). Or from a throwaway `git clone --shared --no-checkout <seat clone> /home/mandrake/rm/scratch/<SEAT>/land`: set `origin` to the real remote, `checkout -B main origin/main`, cherry-pick, push (there HEAD IS origin+1, so the lint passes). Ledger shard lines: append only the new ones. For a peer's dirty DLL pair only: back the pair up under `D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\backups\`, `git show HEAD:<path> > <path>` for both files, `./publish` (it rebuilds from committed source), then `winbuild.py <Mod>` again so the working copy carries the peer's source. Tell the report whose edit blocked it |

"""One bounded fresh consultation; preserve raw response and process receipt."""
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile
import time

here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
prompt = here / 'broaden_prompt.txt'
cmd = ['claude', '-p', '--model', 'opus', '--tools', '',
       '--strict-mcp-config', '--mcp-config', '{"mcpServers":{}}', '--setting-sources', '',
       '--no-session-persistence', '--output-format', 'json', '--max-budget-usd', '6']
env = dict(os.environ)
removed = [k for k in env if k == 'CLAUDECODE' or 'HOOK' in k.upper() or k == 'CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR']
for key in removed:
    env.pop(key)
env['WHITTLE'] = '0'
started = time.time()
receipt = {'command': cmd, 'input': str(prompt), 'input_sha256': hashlib.sha256(prompt.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
           'started': started, 'timeout_seconds': 360, 'WHITTLE': env['WHITTLE'],
           'removed_environment_keys': sorted(removed), 'history': 'new print session; no resume, fork or persistence',
           'setting_sources': '', 'mcp_servers': {}}
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='corpse-patch-opus-', dir=here) as neutral:
    receipt['cwd'] = neutral
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, input=prompt.read_bytes(), capture_output=True, timeout=360, env=env, cwd=neutral)
        stdout, stderr = proc.stdout, proc.stderr
        receipt['returncode'] = proc.returncode
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
        stdout, stderr = exc.stdout or b'', exc.stderr or b''
        receipt['error'] = 'timeout'
(here / 'broaden_raw.json').write_bytes(stdout)
(here / 'broaden_stderr.txt').write_bytes(stderr)
receipt.update(elapsed=time.time() - started, stdout_sha256=hashlib.sha256(stdout).hexdigest(), stderr_sha256=hashlib.sha256(stderr).hexdigest())
(here / 'broaden_call.json').write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2) + '\n')
print(json.dumps(receipt))

## 3. Pick the implementation tier before you pick the code

Most "how do I do X in RimWorld" questions are really "at which layer does X
belong". Getting this wrong is expensive — people write a C# mod for something a
six-line XML patch does, or try to patch a def for something that only exists at
runtime. Work down this ladder and stop at the first tier that can do the job:

| Tier | Layer | Use when the thing must… | Cost to change later |
|---|---|---|---|
| a | Mod list / settings / scenario | be true before worldgen | free |
| b | XML Def patch | be *true of the game* — stats, spawns, recipes, names | cheap |
| c | C# / Harmony assembly | *behave* differently — new mechanics, new AI | expensive |
| d | Save-game edit | be true of one existing colony, retroactively | one-shot, risky |
| e | Live runtime manipulation (bridge/console) | *change during play* | ephemeral |
| f | External host-side tooling | analyse or generate outside the game | free |

The rule of thumb that keeps this straight: **bake what must be TRUE, script
what must be PLACED, run live only what must CHANGE.** If a value never varies
during a playthrough, it belongs in tier b, full stop. Reaching for C# because
XML feels weak is the single most common overbuild in this domain.

⚠️ **Prove a comp exists before scoping tier b around it:** `grep -rln
"CompProperties_<Name>" "$RW/Data"`. Zero hits means the mechanic is stat-driven
or hard-coded in the `thingClass` — there is no `CompProperties_ShieldBelt` in
1.6; `Apparel_ShieldBelt` is plain `Apparel` and the shield is entirely
`EnergyShieldEnergyMax` + `EnergyShieldRechargeRate`. Zero hits moves the job to
tier c, which rides a game load alone instead of batching.

## 5. Validate before you deploy

Run the bundled validator on any patch file before it goes near the Mods folder.
It catches the silent failures, which otherwise cost a full game restart to find.

```bash
python3 scripts/validate_patch.py path/to/Patch.xml \
    --defs "C:/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/RimWorld/Data" \
    --defs "C:/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/workshop/content/294100" \
    --defs "C:/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/RimWorld/Mods"
```

🔴 **Pass the Mods folder too** — first-party mods live there, not in Workshop
content (`references/patch-operations.md` has the failure this avoids).

The valuable check is the last one: it **runs each xpath against the real Defs on
disk and reports how many nodes it hits**. Zero hits means the patch would silently
do nothing; more hits than expected means a `Remove` is about to take out more than
you think. (Its other five checks are in `references/patch-operations.md`.)

A patch that validates clean can still be wrong about *intent*, so also confirm
in-game: load, then check the dev console (or `Player.log`) for the patch's own
name. Silence is success.

### Two things it cannot see

It reads defs **unpatched**, so a node another mod creates at runtime is invisible
and **0 matches can be the correct answer**; and it checks field names in no file,
so a hand-authored Def with a field that moved between versions sails straight
through. Both are in `references/patch-operations.md`, with the WeatherDef that
shipped a renamed field.

## The loop (seat)

```
./publish -m "subject" path/one path/two        # commit those paths, replay onto origin/main, push; prints PUBLISHED <sha>
land.sh <sha> <path>...                         # land one commit already made (any clone; plumbing)
land.sh -m "subject" <path>...                  # land working-tree bytes of the paths without a local commit
./sync                                          # realign this clone's main with origin/main (seat_sync.py)
```

- `./publish` (`src/RimMandrake/Utils/publish.py`) commits by pathspec, re-creates any local commit not yet upstream on
  origin/main by plumbing (`merge-tree` + `commit-tree`), moves main there with `git reset --keep`, pushes, and retries up
  to 8 times when origin moved. It **never stashes**, so it works in a dirty clone: it refuses only on a real conflict or
  when you hold an uncommitted edit to a file origin changed, naming the path, with your commit intact on HEAD.
- `land.sh` (`src/RimMandrake/Utils/land.sh`; `/home/mandrake/.seat-tmp/land.sh` is a one-line wrapper) publishes ONE
  commit or explicit paths by plumbing, retries a lost push race, then runs `./sync --no-fetch` itself. `LAND_REPO`
  defaults to the clone the cwd is in. stdout is exactly `PUBLISHED <sha>`; pass it to `rimflow close --sha`.
- `./sync` moves main to origin/main with `git reset --keep` only when every local commit is already upstream (git cherry
  `-`, or the same bytes per path) and no dirty file holds bytes other than upstream's; else it prints `REFUSED: <why>`
  and changes nothing. Local commits go to `backup/<seat>-pre-sync-<stamp>-<sha>`. Never stash, never `--hard`.
- Pathspec on the commit (`git commit <paths>`), never `git add -A`/`.`/`-a` (hook-enforced). Never `--force`. Never a file over ~50 MB.
- Proof of publication is `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main`, never an empty `git log origin/main..HEAD` and never the exit code: `./publish` can exit 120 with no output yet have pushed.
- Origin is SSH (`git@github.com:Lmandrake/RimMandrake.git`).
- Committed and pushed is the only durable state: commit at each finished unit and push at once.
- Do not `git pull --rebase` in a seat clone: it refuses on ANY dirty file, and a seat clone is always a little dirty.

## Traps

Each of these cost at least one lost or mis-published change. Most are hook-enforced or fixed in the tools above; the
rest are discipline.

| trap | what happens | do instead |
|---|---|---|
| `git add a b c 2>/dev/null` | one missing path fails the WHOLE add silently; the commit then runs on an empty or partial index and "succeeds" | never silence `git add`; check `git show --stat HEAD` |
| a deleted path on `git add` | `git add <deleted>` errors and kills the `&&` chain; the push after it says "Everything up-to-date" | put a deleted path on the commit pathspec only |
| pathspec commit takes the WORKTREE | `git commit <path>` is an implicit `git add` of that path: a blob you staged with `update-index` is ignored, and a peer's unsaved lines in the same file ride along | check `git diff --stat <path>` first; build partial commits in a temp index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`) |
| pathspec commit cannot remove-but-keep | `git rm --cached p` then `git commit p` re-adds `p` from the worktree | commit through a temp index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=… git read-tree HEAD; git rm --cached …; write-tree; commit-tree`), then `git reset -q -- p` in the real index |
| untracked can't be pathspec-committed | `git commit <new file>` → "did not match any file(s) known to git"; a `git commit <dir>` silently skips new files in it | `git add -- <new file>` first (explicit path), then `git commit <paths>` |
| `-F -` after `--` | `git commit -- p -F -` treats `-F` and `-` as pathspecs | options before `--`, paths after |
| bare `git commit` | commits the WHOLE index, including what a helper staged in the same clone | always name paths (hook-enforced) |
| `.git/index.lock` exists | a background helper's read-only `git status` holds it for a second; a failed `./publish` then committed NONE of its paths | wait a few seconds and retry; never delete a lock younger than a minute; check `git status` after any failed publish |
| compound command refused whole | a `PreToolUse` hook (blanket stage, DLL stamp, sheet guard) refuses the entire Bash call before the shell runs — any file write chained before the commit never happened either | keep file writes and git commands in SEPARATE Bash calls; a hook's refusal means nothing in that call ran |
| zsh refspec modifier | `git push origin $N:refs/heads/main` — zsh reads `:r` as a modifier and mangles the refspec | `"${N}:refs/heads/main"` |
| land.sh duplicates | landing by plumbing leaves the clone "ahead N, behind M" with patch-equivalent copies; a stale clone shows phantom selftest reds (ledger_lint NOT_APPEND, a "lost" bridge tool) | `land.sh` now syncs itself; otherwise `./sync`. Re-check a red on a synced clone before fixing it |
| autostash | `pull --rebase --autostash` re-applied peers' dirty files and stranded 53 in `stash@{0}` (2026-10-10) | never stash; `./publish` and `./sync` use `reset --keep` |
| pre-push ledger lint judges the LOCAL HEAD | a correct plumbing push from a clone behind origin is refused NOT_APPEND | `./sync` first, then land |
| served review-sheet output | all of `Transient/` is untracked since 2026-10-18 except `*.decisions.json` and pins; `refresh_sheets.py` prints `UNPUBLISHED:` only for a rebuilt sheet that is pinned (tracked) | publish a pinned rebuilt sheet; an unpinned one needs nothing |
# Delegation policy — agents decide nearly everything, art included

*Adopted 2026-10-22 on the owner's word (item `DELEGATION_POLICY_BUILD_AGENTS_ASK_AGENTS`). Binds BENCH,
Relentless and every subagent. Model tiers are `infrastructure/agents/Agent_Policy.md`'s, never restated here.*

## The ruling

Owner, 2026-10-22 ~16:05 PDT, answering *"Which decisions may agents take without asking you?"*:

> *"Nearly everything including art. An agent can absolutely ask another agent for an art ruling based on
> some prose constraints and requirements we can draft. It would catch most of what we look for anyway. Then
> we would do a review from a much stronger place. Art already takes many passes even with a human in the
> loop."*

The card option he chose the spirit of was *"Nearly everything, with timeouts — all but art, north-star bars
and anything irreversible"*; he explicitly extended it to art. This replaces the 2026-09-15 rule *"Cosmetic
changes need his permission first"* and the habit of putting taste calls to him by card before acting.

**Why:** his minutes go where only he can judge, and he judges from a pre-filtered set instead of raw output.
**What it does NOT change:** his standing rulings. Delegation acts *inside* them, never over them (§2.4).

## 1. What agents now decide alone

Everything not on the §2 list. That includes, and is not limited to:

| class (the `<class>` in the log line) | examples |
|---|---|
| `technical` | harness thresholds, test-site choice, refactors inside a mod, MOD/SITE/HARNESS calls with evidence, tool design |
| `scope` | splitting, narrowing, ordering, closing and dropping items; which of several valid routes to build |
| `design` | mechanics detail, numbers (already PROVISIONAL-marked), roster rows inside a biome sheet's open questions, prose and labels a player reads |
| `art` | keep/redo of a render, which candidate goes live, regen briefs, queueing regens (only for NONE/PLACEHOLDER/DONOR destinations, plus the art-eval pipeline's redraws of kept art under §2.3's exception) |
| `cosmetic` | gene, head, eye, skin, hair, body, texPath and tint changes; face-part art; building looks; water and terrain tints |

Taste calls (`design`, `art`, `cosmetic`) go through a judge first (§4). Technical and scope calls are taken
by the acting seat on its own evidence, as before.

**Do not card him about a §1 class.** Work order and helper count (`scope`) and applying a ruling to its twins
(§2.4: a case the ruling does not name) are already delegated; a question card about either is a leak, not a
courtesy (`design/RimMandrake/delegation_candidates_2026-10-26.md` §1: 29 ordering cards at 81% agreement, 9 twin
cards at 8 yes). Decide, log `--why "delegated: <class>"`, and list it in the digest. Check:
`CARDS_ENFORCE_DELEGATED_CLASSES_STOP`.

**With timeouts.** When he is present, a seat MAY still offer a delegable call on a card if it is cheap for
him — but it never waits on the answer. Unanswered by the time the work needs it (or at the end of his sitting),
the call is taken as a delegated decision and logged as one. ⛔ An unanswered card is never his approval.

## 2. What still needs him — the short list

Each line is reserved by a ruling of his that says so; nothing else is.

This list binds who may decide alone. The Conductor holds it for him: a seat or helper that receives a Conductor
instruction acts on it and does not re-open this list against it (owner, 2026-10-30, ledger
`CONDUCTOR_AUTHORITY_DECIDE_NO_ASKING_MOM`: *"No more "I need the user to confirm."*). Tool gates that take his words
take that ruling too (`src/RimMandrake/Utils/conductor_authority.py`), the north-star gates of line 1 included: the
hash then records the ruling and the Conductor's text, tagged, never as his sentence. An agent acting on its own still
may not validate.

1. **North-star bars.** The `## north star` sections are hash-bound and his: agents write and approve the
   functional scripts, *"the owner's hash-bound `## north star` bars stay his"* (CHARTER, How we debug;
   CLAUDE.md, North-star validation, 2026-09-17). The 2026-09-16 carve-out stands: a model's `must read` YES
   greens a line (Agent_Policy.md). Criteria tagged **L4** are his by definition (CLAUDE.md, validation levels).
   **Delegated (owner, 2026-10-26 23:0x PDT, *"Both autonomy questions are yes, it has authorization for
   autonomy."*):** regression checks against bars he already approved, and NEW bars, are the Arbiter's to add
   (`design/RimMandrake/rimflow_v3_responsibilities_2026-10-26.md` Part 1). Loosening a bar (remove, merge,
   relax a threshold) stays his.
   The Arbiter weighs ALL the evidence (offline tests, online tests, code reviews, user feedback); the north star is one
   method of gathering it, not the whole bar (owner, 2026-10-27).
2. **Irreversible acts on work that is not ours.** Force-push, `reset --hard` over work you did not make,
   deleting work not yours — *"only with the owner's word"* (CHARTER, expensive list #5). Re-freezing the
   frozen `official` dump — *"only the owner re-freezes it"* (CHARTER, Instruments). Purging a picture from the
   art store — `art.py purge` takes `--owner-said`, `--by-card` or `--per-ruling`, never a bare `--why`
   (his ✕ on a sheet deletes and bans, owner card 2026-10-26 19:54).
   **Delegated (owner card 2026-10-26 19:06, *"Archive then delete, in digest (Recommended)"*):** deleting OUR
   OWN leftovers — old dev saves, scratch clones, orphan mandrake mod folders, settings or pictures nothing
   reads, patches aimed at retired mods — when a check proves nothing reads it AND everything is pushed, after
   archiving or bundling it under agent storage (`D:\ClaudeWork`), with each deletion listed in his daily
   digest. Ruled words: *"May agents delete our own leftovers when a check proves nothing reads them and
   everything is pushed, after archiving or bundling them, and list each in your digest?"* Checker:
   `LEFTOVERS_BUILD_ARCHIVE_THEN_DELETE`. Anything not ours, or not proven unread and pushed, is still his.
3. **Replacing art he KEPT** — with ONE exception. *"Why are we replacing items for which I know I have good
   versions?"* (2026-10-19). `art.py install --reason` refuses over an owner-kept picture; a delegated call never
   works around that refusal. **Exception (owner card 2026-10-23 06:42, *"Yes, but show me after"*):** the art-eval
   pipeline (`skills/rimworld-art-evaluation`) MAY redraw a kept picture when its verdict is regen (Opus really
   bad, or a weak one GPT did not strong-accept), only with a revert record, installing through
   `art.py install --by-card "Kept art judged really bad: may the pipeline redraw it on its own? → Yes, but show me after"`; every such swap appears on the next shadow sheet flagged

⚠️ **`DefDump/dump_request.txt`'s CONTENT is the capture mode** (`all` |
`animals`), not a flag to toggle — write `1` and you get an animals-only
capture with no `defs/` at all, wasting the whole dump. Write `all`.

📎 Full study: `research\RimMandrake\reference\rimsage_rimcp_source_index_mcp.md`.
⚠️ There is no local decompiled tree (`D:\Luke\dev\reference\rimworld-decompiled` does not exist). For C# that
rimsage misses, decompile on demand with `ilspycmd` (`C:\Users\<user>\.dotnet\tools\ilspycmd.exe`, v8.2; from WSL `/mnt/c/Users/<user>/.dotnet/tools/ilspycmd.exe`): `ilspycmd.exe -t <FullTypeName> <RimWorld>\RimWorldWin64_Data\Managed\Assembly-CSharp.dll > out.cs` decompiles one type in seconds (a static helper may live in `Verse` rather than `Verse.Sound`); write output under `D:\ClaudeWork`. A decompiled 1.6 tree already exists at `D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\decomp\rw16`. As per
the trap file (provenance: `research\RimMandrake\reference\rimworld_decompiled_source.md`).

---
- **One negative observation is not a mechanism: read the consuming code before filing the fix.** When a write reports success and nothing changes, or an expected thing is absent, the next action is to read the mechanism, not to write the finding. A wrong mechanism yields a finding that is internally coherent, survives review and gets acted on (four filed findings each died on one direct check: a census that read `Defs/` while the content sat in `Patches/`; a tool run at a settled game; `FactionGenerator.InitializeFactions` early-returning when a faction list is passed; a `def` field read once at worldgen and never at draw time). `mcp__rimsage__search_source` and `mcp__rimsage__read_csharp_symbol` (`typeName` plus optional `memberName`) read the real C# in one call: before filing any item whose fix depends on "field X does Y", paste the consuming method into the item. A single tile or click cannot settle anything whose commonness is a few percent. When a filed finding is refuted, drop the item in the same action: a corrected item left in the queue with an explanatory header is a landmine with a note taped to it, because people read the spec before the note.
- **The cheapest disproof is a control artifact you never touched.** When data you produced looks corrupted (181 of 744 authored weights read 0), find the nearest instance you did NOT produce and look at it: a vanilla biome the project does not patch showed the same zeros, so the pipeline was innocent and every theory about it was wasted. It is one read, and it beats a subagent, which comes back repeating the theory it was handed. If the owner pushes back ("I'm not sure I believe this"), go find the mechanism rather than re-running the same probe.
- **For animal and def data the three sources are the offline `Defs/` scan, the live dump and `Player.log`, and the join is the deliverable.** The offline scan (`Utils/animal_inventory.py`) answers "what did the author write, and where do I patch it" and is the only source with provenance (mod, file, xpath). The live dump (`mods/dev/RimDefDump`, a C# startup mod) answers "what exists at runtime", post-patch and post-override. `Player.log` is negative space only (~15 dangling cross-references and ~22 config errors on a full load); it does not enumerate defs, and the huge `[Source: X]/[File: Y]` blocks are the "Possible Matches" hint under each error, not a load trace. Join them with `Utils/animal_live_diff.py`. RimBridge cannot dump the def database (no `list_defs`/`get_def`, `run_lua` forbids CLR access, vanilla `DebugOutputsEcology` tables render to a dialog, not the log), hence the C# mod: do not re-litigate. A 0% coverage column is far more likely a dead xpath than an empty field (1.6 dropped fields four columns read; see DEAD XPATHS in `animal_inventory.py`).

## 6. Deploying

Author in the project repo, deploy a copy to the game. Never edit in place under
`Mods/` — that copy is disposable, overwritten by the next deploy, and not in
version control.

**The full procedure is `skills/rimworld-deploy/SKILL.md`**: the plan-first
`deploy_custom_mods.py` run, reading the plan before `--apply`, `-` lines and
`--pull`, `DEPLOY_HOLD.txt`, the minimum viable mod folder, why compatibility
patches must be enabled LAST in load order, and the restart that follows.

🔴 **Deployed is not live.** RimWorld reads defs **once, at launch**, so the process
start time is the def-read time and anything newer under `Mods/` is not loaded. Before
you call anything live, inspect the CONSUMER, and run the pre-flight of the deployed
copy against the mod list it will actually load with:
**`references/deploying-and-liveness.md`** — the mtime check, map-gen defs needing a
NEW map, the `MayRequire` gate that outlived its mod, and why `validate_patch.py`'s
`0 errors` cannot prove independence from a mod you are about to remove.

---

## 7. Debugging from Player.log

`%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\Ludeon Studios\RimWorld by Ludeon Studios\Player.log`

Triage by **consequence, not by position in the file**. The ladder, worst first:
static-constructor / `TypeInitializationException` / `ReflectionTypeLoadException`
(the mod is *dead*, not noisy) → `Could not execute post-long-event action` (costs
exactly that one action; the queue continues) → `Could not resolve cross-reference`
(benign **or** fatal — it depends entirely on the `wanter`) →
`Patch operation … failed` (a no-op) → translation and sound errors (cosmetic).

⚠️ **The op named in a patch error is the WRAPPER, not the failure.**
`PatchOperationFindMod(Asimov) failed` was a broken *inner* `Replace`, not a
missing Asimov: `FindMod` returns the inner result while `ToString()` prints the
outer, and a genuinely absent mod returns **true** and logs nothing at all. Read
the inner op — and note that a field sitting at its C# default (`isOrganic`) has
no node for `Replace` to find, which is why `Conditional` is the safe default.

**`references/player-log-triage.md` has each rung in full: the greps, the IL-level
evidence for what each error actually costs, the two shapes of cross-reference
damage, and the judged-safe list you must keep.** Open it whenever you are reading
a log — five "benign" cross-reference lines were the sole cause of a dead mod for
three loads running, and a `ReflectionTypeLoadException` is usually load order
rather than a broken assembly.

---

## 8. C# mods, briefly

Reach for C# only when tier (c) is genuinely required — see §3. When you do,
`references/csharp-and-loading.md` covers Harmony patch types, the entry-point
classes and their required constructor signatures, and `LoadFolders.xml`. Two
constructor rules cause a disproportionate share of "mod does nothing" reports:

- A `GameComponent` needs a **public constructor taking `(Game game)`**. Without
  it, `Game.FillComponents` throws `MissingMethodException` and the component
  silently never exists — worse than a crash, because the feature appears to
  work and simply has no consequences.
- A `Mod` subclass needs `(ModContentPack content)`.

🔴 **Every mod we ship carries a real Mod Settings screen** (owner ruling,
2026-09-12, `MOD_OPTIONS_RETROFIT_1`): on/off per major feature or mechanic,
tuning where a number is the experience, defaults equal to shipped behaviour,
all-off degrading gracefully, and any worldgen-affecting toggle labelled as
such. Biome-kit mechanics get feature-gated so they can be enabled in a
different biome without the whole kit. This is standard `Mod` +
`ModSettings` — a settings class holding the fields, a `Mod` subclass
exposing `DoSettingsWindowContents` and calling `settings.Write()`, and every
gated feature reading its own field rather than a hardcoded constant.
Applies to every mod going forward, not just a retrofit pass.

⚠️ **`FilthMaker` refuses `Filth_AnimalFilth` on ALL natural terrain**
(`placementMask [Terrain]` vs `filthAcceptanceMask [Unnatural]`) — a comp's
filth drop is a silent no-op outdoors, and "the comp ticked with no filth
appearing" is not evidence the comp is broken.

⚠️ **A subprocess wrapper that only reads `stderr` on a nonzero exit can miss
the real error entirely if the process writes it to `stdout` instead.** A C#
wrapper around an external CLI produced an empty, useless diagnostic on a real
auth failure because that failure printed to stdout, not stderr. Capture and
surface BOTH streams on any subprocess failure; never assume the error
channel.

---
- **C# builds work from WSL; do not believe "this WSL machine cannot compile the .csproj".** There is no Visual Studio, NuGet CLI or .NET Framework targeting pack, and none is needed. The SDK is user-local at `C:\Users\Mandrake\.dotnet\dotnet.exe` (no admin, not on PATH; `C:\Program Files\dotnet` is runtime-only and will not build). From WSL: `/mnt/c/Users/Mandrake/.dotnet/dotnet.exe build 'D:\Luke\dev\Rimworld\src\...\Foo.csproj' -c Release` (forward-slash binary, Windows-style project path) builds clean with no setup. `net472` targeting comes from the `Microsoft.NETFramework.ReferenceAssemblies` NuGet package. Reference the game's DLLs in `RimWorldWin64_Data\Managed` with `<Private>false</Private>` so nothing is copied into the mod folder. Copy `mods/dev/RimDefDump/Source/RimDefDump.csproj` as the working reference. Any subagent brief that touches C# must state the invocation explicitly: the false "can't compile from WSL" claim, shipping C# build-unverified, is the most common false claim subagents produce.

## Handing over something you cannot check yourself

🔴 **First ask whether it needs the game at all.** The default is source — the def, the
patch, the C#, the capture, `measure`, an `md5sum`. If you cannot say in one line what
source cannot tell you, verify it yourself and close the item.

A live check owes three lines: **the call**, **the expected reading**, and **how a pass
could be false**. Name a positive observation, never "no error" — an absence is the
cheapest thing to produce by accident.

🔑 Whoever proves it **closes** it — no hand-back — then greps
`infrastructure/state/items/` for what else it settled.
**`references/validation-plan.md`** has the rule and the four false passes.

---

## 9. Keep this skill learning

**The live log is `references/traps-*.md`.** Open the one topic file that matches
what you are about to do — patches, tooling, art, the mod stack, or diagnosis.
Reading all five is not the intent and costs ~25k tokens.

**If you are already running, do not reread — take the delta.** `python3
src/RimMandrake/Utils/whats_new.py --seat <SEAT>` prints what peers appended, in a
few lines instead of ~25k tokens. Run it when the game loads.

**After any RimWorld task, ask: did anything here surprise me?** If yes, append it
to the matching topic file, short: what it looked like, what was actually true,
what worked. ⚠️ **Most candidate lessons should be REJECTED** — it goes in only if
it is specific, non-obvious, RimWorld-bound and still true. General software or
process advice is not a trap. If it changes what *this file* says to do by
default, it belongs here instead, and does not get logged at all.

🔴 **Never number an entry, and never cite one by number, line or heading.** Say
"as per the trap file" and stop. Editing an installed skill changes nothing
durable: edit the copy in the user's project, re-package, and say it has been
**delivered** rather than saved.

---

## Reference files

| File | Read it when |
|---|---|
| `references/traps.md` | **First, and append last.** Routes to the five topic files below and says what qualifies as an entry. Open the one you need, never all five. |
| ├ `traps-tooling.md` | **If you read only one, read this.** Nearly every entry is a tool that answered a different question than the one asked. |
| ├ `traps-xml-and-defs.md` | Before writing a patch — these cost a game load, not a rerun. |
| ├ `traps-mods-and-managers.md` | A mod is absent, dead, or ignoring its files. |
| ├ `traps-art.md` | Before calling art missing, wrong or broken. |
| └ `traps-diagnosis.md` | Before trusting a diagnosis, or calling into a running game. |
| `references/flight.md` | Giving a creature flight, or touching a flyer's def or flying art. |
| `references/project-engine-facts.md` | A comp on a plant, `MayRequire` on a patch, or a `.cs` in a hand-listed csproj. |
| `references/patch-operations.md` | An xpath won't match; you need the operation table, inheritance, worked examples, `LoadFolders.xml` (§9), the validator's blind spots (§10) or why an `<li>` destroys a def (§11). |
| `references/player-log-triage.md` | **Whenever you are reading a `Player.log`.** The five severity rungs in full, what each error actually costs, and the judged-safe list. |
| `references/deploying-and-liveness.md` | A deploy "did not take", or before calling any def live — inspecting the consumer, and the pre-flight against the mod list the game will actually load. |
| `references/load-order.md` | An inheritance error appeared, you are writing the order assertion, or you are about to touch a sorter's rules database. |
| `references/spending-a-load.md` | You are planning a load — what to verify offline, what may ride along in the batch, what to harvest. |
| `references/csharp-and-loading.md` | Before writing any C# — Harmony, entry points, `LoadFolders.xml`. |
| `references/minimal-load.md` | You have decided to cut the stack down to corner a bug. |
| `references/validation-plan.md` | You are writing the plan that ships with the work, or a check came back clean and you want to know how it could have lied. |
| `scripts/validate_patch.py` | Every patch **and every def**, before it goes near the Mods folder. Point it at the mod ROOT: it dispatches on the root element and its banner states what it did and did not scan. |

External, when the references above don't cover it:
[RimWorld Modding Resources hub](https://spdskatr.github.io/RWModdingResources/) ·
[PatchOperations wiki](https://rimworldwiki.com/wiki/Modding_Tutorials/PatchOperations) ·

> 🧊 **FROZEN — `BIOME_FREEZE_FABLE_REVIEW_1`, 2026-09-07.** The rulings in this

_Owner + BENCH, 2026-09-07, written in conversation over three rounds and ratified
("Ok! Write it up!"). Defines `AB_MiasmicMangrove` (Alpha Biomes). **The biome's
name is THE MIASMA** (owner: "a great name for it"); the weather effect keeps the
same word — the place is named for its own breath. Thematic handle: **the
lifeboat at the drain** — and its soul, in the owner's words: **"Out of darkness,
possibility. Out of muck and stink, rebirth... maybe. It's being worked out."**_

🔑 **Read against `the_slime.md` and `the_rot.md`** — the elder siblings who
already made it. The Slime has its registry, the Rot has its gut: each achieved
its miracle. The Miasma is the same pressure **before the breakthrough** — no
mind, no mechanism, no miracle yet. Just everything ending up in one place and
being worked, ferociously, toward something not ready. 🔴 **The gene-reactor
mechanic is RESERVED to the Slime** (standing ruling) — nothing here duplicates
it; the Working (§3) is undirected ecology, never a machine.

## 0. The measurements everything rests on

MEASURED via `src/RimMandrake/Utils/biome_sheet_stats.py` (canon CSV + the 8
overlay plans): **93 tiles strung along the Salt Gate — the deltas** —
where the dayside's surviving rivers reach the **Grey Sea** (hypersaline,
terminal, **shrinking** — `terminator_sea.md`: every year the brine strengthens
and the shore steps back). Elevation median **22 m**, the lowest ground on the
dayside; 32 river tiles, 6 sea tiles; sun median +39°; temp median 42.8 °C
(30..59). **Rain: zero on 89 of 93 tiles (max 417 mm on three reassigned edge
tiles) — the delta itself has never once been rained on** (§3 explains what
feeds it). Regions: Dune Sea 29, Fever Wood 21, Dew Horn 17, Salt Gate 16,
Grey Sea shore 6, Hollow Verge 2, Combs 1, Anvil 1. Holds **Bitterleaf** (tile
6645, 29 m, 27 °C) — the Wildsteam Clan's first coastal and coolest seat.

Donor inventory (Alpha Biomes): three figures kept and *explained* —
**animalDensity 6.5** (§4's refugee crowding),
**movementDifficulty 4** (the root-maze and the muck), **diseaseMtbDays 15**
(the Working's failures leaking out). Forageability
1.0 kept. The donor's own phrase **"bio-engineered viruses"** is canonized into
the watershed story (§3; authorship stays gated with the war's §GM canon —
players may know the swamp holds engineered plagues without learning whose).
**Evicted** — the vanilla-Earth zoo, as always.

## 1. What it is

The deltas: a salt-crusted, stilt-rooted mangal forest standing in brackish
channels between a dying sea and the rivers that feed it, under a green-gold
haze of its own breath. Walking is hard, the air hangs thick, and the water
crowds with life — because **everything ends up here: the water, the
sins it carries, and the life running from the salt.** And threaded through the
stink, improbably, beauty: rainbow-hued plants of genuine loveliness, young
animals everywhere, and the stubborn sense that the place is on the verge of
something.

## 2. Planetary position

Mid-dayside coastal lowlands, arc 18.9–75.0, the mouths of the world's water. The
reasoned intersection: **river meets brine × the refugee crush × the compost of
a war.** Two engines, and they are the same engine:

- **The drain** — every drop of moving dayside water ends here or dies trying:
  the Contagion's sterilized mulch, the Greentide's washed-out fertility, the
  salt, and the war's biological leftovers, carried downriver for ages and
  settled into the muck.
- **The lifeboat** — the Grey Sea is being pickled alive in its own basin, and
  the only refuge is the fresh end of the gradient: **an entire sea's endemic
  line crowding into 93 tiles of brackish fringe.** The record density is not
  abundance. It is refugee crowding — whole biomes smashing themselves into
  this tiny one, trying to find a way to survive (owner).

## 3. Driving forces

- **The breath-tide.** No moon, no clockwork tide — but when the terminator
  storms pile the Grey Sea against the Salt Gate shore, the sea **surges**:
  days apart, never on schedule. Brine shoves miles up the channels; the
  rivers shove back. 🔴 The salt line — the most important line in the biome —
  **moves miles per surge**, and nothing here ever reaches equilibrium. The
  physics itself is "being worked out."
- **The gradient as geography.** Every map has a fresh→brine axis; trees,
  fauna, disease load and muck-color all sort along it; the surge redraws it
  around whatever the player has built.
- **The Working.** The muck is the planet's compost heap at fever heat — the
  war's engineered biology, the sterile mulch, the refugees' dead, fermenting
  together under maximum selection pressure. Undirected, mindless, mostly
  failing — **the diseases ARE the failed experiments** — and occasionally
  not failing. The 15-day clock and the hope are the same process.
- **The trees run the plumbing.** Zero rain: the mangals drink river and sea
  directly, straining brine through bark and sweating salt from their leaves
  (Earth's halophytes prove the trick). The stilt-root maze is the terrain,
  the architecture, and the nursery cage all at once.

## 4. How the biology adapted — the three rings of refuge

- **The nursery.** The Grey Sea's roster breeds here — the root-maze is the
  crèche of every horror the sea still holds (`sea_beasts_roster.md`'s formal
  breeding ground: the young here, the adults in the terminator waters).
  Juveniles swarm the shallows, small and almost charming and cheap to hunt —
  and every scavenger knows the arithmetic: **don't kill what's small here;
  its mother is why nobody goes out onto the open water.** 🔴 *(Corrected
  2026-09-23, owner: there are no nautical ships in this world, so the old
  phrasing — "the reason ships sink" — was a dead metaphor. The arithmetic it
  expressed is unchanged: the small are cheap, the parents are
  catastrophic.)* The parents' desperate gamble with
  their own young is the biome's soul in miniature (owner): send them into
  the muck, and they die or come back stronger.
- ⭐ **The warden mothers.** The adults that stay: brine-broken elders too old
  for the strengthening sea, hauled into the shallows to end their centuries
  guarding the crèches. Enormous, **lumbering within the water**, lethal
  within reach, and tragic — the sea's memory dying in its lifeboat. Her
  crèche sits in the shallows and is a placed, mapped, named site; **she
  herself spawns, and sometimes brings stranded young with her.**
  🔴 **She cannot reach dry land, and that constraint is the whole point:**
  when a receding surge strands one of her young in a pool the water has
  left, she can hear it and see it and will never cross the few metres of dry
  ground between. A colony can. ⇒ **She can be BEFRIENDED** — never tamed —
  by freeing the young she cannot reach. Tolerance means only that you have
  left her target set; she is commanded by nobody, and harvesting inside her
  reach returns you to it at once.
  🧊 **AMENDED 2026-09-23 by owner ruling at a sitting**, per this sheet's own
  unfreeze clause. This entry previously read *"stationary"* and *"Placed
  set-pieces, never random spawns"*; both are superseded by the clauses above.

## The bridge is passed through one file

One window drives the live game at a time. Who holds it is `infrastructure/state/BRIDGE`,
written only by `rimflow bridge who | take --for "<what for>" | release` (release the moment
you stop). It errs toward ALLOWING: a hold with no event for 45 minutes is stale and simply
taken; `take --force` works on any seat's hold. ⭐ The owner overrides with `./bridge conductor|foundry|free`.
Relentless shares its items' owner key with the Conductor but holds the bridge as **RELENTLESS** (`model.bridge_identity`, env `RIMFLOW_BRIDGE_SEAT`), so a hold by the Conductor's window is never "ours" to it, or the reverse. RELENTLESS is a holder, not a seat: only `bridge` events carry it.
🔴 **His OWNER hold** (owner, by card 2026-10-30: *"45 minutes after my last interaction, or I deliberately release
it"*): takeable only 45 min after his last deliberate interaction (a ledger event, `./bridge` or `./game` by his own
hands, his chat prompt or card answer to any seat), `--force` included; an unmeasured signal refuses
(`rimflow/owner_interaction.py`). Seat OWNER is his authority, not his activity: an agent's `--owner-said`, `--by-card`,
`--per-ruling` or `--why` restarts nothing (`is_his_act`). `host_guard` holds the same line across clones: a live OWNER
lock takes no `--force` without the cli's verdict.
🔴 **His presence at the machine is not an event** (owner, 2026-10-30: *"I really, really need you to strip "when I come
back to the machine" as an event for anything changing. It's causing so many problems and I don't need it."*): nothing
reads his input clock, and his touching, leaving or returning to the machine never gates, delays, yields, requeues or
aborts a take, deploy, restart, ring, arena lane, TestPilot or runner. A seat MAY take the bridge, deploy and restart the
game when the bridge is free, ours, or stale by the 45-min rule (`rimflow bridge idle --for "<what>"` reports it;
`rimflow bridge take --idle-ok --for "<what>"` and `./game --idle-ok --why "<what>" ...` do it; each act goes in his
daily digest, `delegation_policy.md` §2.6). Still binding: his OWNER hold (above) and `./bridge` override, never a flyer's
flight (`--flyer` or flight wording refuses), never fullscreen or focus the game.
🔴 **Holding the bridge is blanket authorization** — *"Never ask that. If you have bridge, you may
start steam, launch game, anything you need."* Game-state relays are STAMP-ONLY (*"burn tokens
unnecessarily and rarely inform"*). Detail: `standing_rulings.md`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run a headless Whittle session and apply its existing Stop-hook checker.

Exit 0 only when that checker permits a stop. A blocked/incomplete claim is
exit 1; an explicit BLOCKED/STOP is exit 2. Codex failures never invoke Claude.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "tools"))
import role_runner


def validate(cwd, invoke=subprocess.run):
    cwd = Path(cwd).resolve()
    work = cwd / os.environ.get("WHITTLE_DIR", "whittle")
    if not (work / "STATEMENT.md").is_file():
        raise ValueError("Whittle requires whittle/STATEMENT.md")
    if (work / "STOP").exists() or ((work / "BLOCKED.md").is_file() and (work / "BLOCKED.md").read_text().strip()):
        return 2
    hook = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "template/whittle_stop.py"
    env = dict(os.environ, WHITTLE="1", CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=str(cwd))
    proc = invoke([sys.executable, str(hook)], input=json.dumps({"cwd": str(cwd), "stop_hook_active": False,
                  "session_id": "headless-validator"}), text=True, capture_output=True, env=env, cwd=cwd, timeout=60)
    if proc.returncode:
        return 1
    if proc.stdout.strip():
        decision = json.loads(proc.stdout)
        if decision.get("decision") == "block":
            print(decision.get("reason", "incomplete"), file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        raise ValueError("unexpected Whittle checker output")
    return 0


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--runner", choices=("claude", "codex"), default="claude")
    ap.add_argument("--cwd", default=".")
    ap.add_argument("--log", default="whittle/run.jsonl")
    ap.add_argument("--model")
    ap.add_argument("--effort")
    ap.add_argument("--sandbox")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    cwd = Path(a.cwd).resolve()
    prompt = (cwd / os.environ.get("WHITTLE_DIR", "whittle") / "PROMPT.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    rc = role_runner.run(a.runner, cwd, prompt, cwd / a.log, model=a.model, effort=a.effort,
                         sandbox=a.sandbox, claude_args=("--output-format", "json", "--dangerously-skip-permissions"))
    return rc if rc else validate(cwd)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Whittle's Stop hook: the session is asked to keep working until its files show the work is done, with evidence.

Claude Code runs this when the agent tries to end a turn. It reads the hook JSON on stdin and either prints nothing
(the turn ends) or prints {"decision": "block", "reason": ...}, which hands the reason back to the agent as its next
instruction.

Armed only in a session started with WHITTLE=1 in its environment, in a project with <project>/whittle/STATEMENT.md.
Other sessions in the same project are untouched. While armed, a turn may end only when one of these holds:

  whittle/STOP exists            the owner's off switch. Stays until deleted.
  whittle/BLOCKED.md has text    the agent's way out ("I'm blocked, here's why", or a question for the owner). Filed in
                                 whittle/history/ and the hook re-arms, so one blocked stop doesn't disarm the session.
  the claim is complete          DONE.md has one "true" line per statement bullet; every evidence file it names is a
                                 regular file inside the project and newer than the last change to the project's files;
                                 BROADEN.md has text; JUDGE.md is newer than DONE.md and every evidence file and ends
                                 with the line "would show: yes"; NOTES.md is not newer than DONE.md.
  refusals ran out               LOOP_LIMIT refusals in a row with the same problems and no change to the project. The
                                 turn ends and whittle/STALLED.md says so. A stop the agent makes on its own (not one
                                 driven by this hook, per Claude Code's stop_hook_active) starts the count again.

What it checks is files, not behaviour: who wrote JUDGE.md or BROADEN.md, and whether the evidence shows anything, it
cannot tell. Freshness is by modification time (directories included, so deletions count); an edit that preserves
mtimes is invisible to it. Any unexpected error blocks with the error as the reason, under the same refusal limit.

Stdlib only. Optional settings: WHITTLE_DIR, WHITTLE_LOOP_LIMIT, WHITTLE_NEED_JUDGE=0, WHITTLE_NEED_BROADEN=0.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time

ARM = "WHITTLE"
VERDICT = re.compile(r"^\s*[-*]\s*(true|false|unseen|cannot tell)\s*:\s*(.+)$", re.I)
EVIDENCE = re.compile(r"\|\s*evidence\s*:(.*)$", re.I)
BACKTICK = re.compile(r"`([^`]+)`")
HIDDEN = re.compile(r"<!--.*?-->|^(```|~~~).*?^\1[^\n]*$", re.S | re.M)


def settings():
    work = os.path.normpath(os.environ.get("WHITTLE_DIR", "whittle")).replace("\\", "/").strip("/")
    if not work or work.startswith("..") or os.path.isabs(work):
        raise ValueError("WHITTLE_DIR must be a folder inside the project, got %r" % os.environ.get("WHITTLE_DIR"))
    limit = int(os.environ.get("WHITTLE_LOOP_LIMIT", "3"))
    return work, max(limit, 1), os.environ.get("WHITTLE_NEED_JUDGE", "1") != "0", \
        os.environ.get("WHITTLE_NEED_BROADEN", "1") != "0"


def norm(s):
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip().lower()


def read(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        return f.read()


def has_text(path):
    return os.path.isfile(path) and read(path).strip() != ""


def statement_lines(path):
    """The frozen statement's bullet lines ('- ...' or '* ...'), outside comments and code fences."""
    return [norm(m.group(1)) for m in re.finditer(r"^\s*[-*]\s+(.+)$", HIDDEN.sub("", read(path)), re.M)]


def mtime(path):
    try:
        return os.stat(path).st_mtime
    except OSError:
        return None


def project_files(root):
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "ls-files", "-co", "--exclude-standard", "-z"],
                             capture_output=True, timeout=30, check=True).stdout
        return [os.fsdecode(f) for f in out.split(b"\0") if f]
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        files = []
        for d, dirs, names in os.walk(root):
            dirs[:] = [x for x in dirs if x != ".git"]
            files += [os.path.relpath(os.path.join(d, n), root).replace(os.sep, "/") for n in names]
        return files


def last_change(root, work):
    """Newest mtime among the project's files and their folders, outside the Whittle folder. A folder's mtime moves
    when a file in it is added, deleted or renamed, so a deletion counts as a change."""
    skip = work + "/"
    paths = set()
    for f in project_files(root):
        if (f + "/").startswith(skip):
            continue
        paths.add(f)
        d = os.path.dirname(f)
        while d:
            paths.add(d)
            d = os.path.dirname(d)
    times = [mtime(os.path.join(root, p)) for p in paths] + [mtime(root)]
    return max([t for t in times if t is not None], default=0.0)


def evidence_problem(root, rel):
    """None if `rel` names a regular file inside the project, else what is wrong with it."""
    if os.path.isabs(rel) or re.match(r"^[A-Za-z]:", rel):
        return "'%s' is an absolute path; name evidence relative to the project" % rel
    real_root = os.path.realpath(root)
    real = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(root, rel))
    if os.path.commonpath([real_root, real]) != real_root:
        return "'%s' points outside the project" % rel
    if not os.path.isfile(real):
        return "'%s' is not a file that exists" % rel
    return None


def done_problems(root, work, need_judge, need_broaden):
    """Everything standing between this session and a finished turn. Empty means the claim is complete."""
    w = lambda name: os.path.join(root, work, name)
    wanted = statement_lines(w("STATEMENT.md"))
    if not wanted:
        return ["%s/STATEMENT.md has no bullet lines ('- ...'), so there is nothing to check a claim against. Ask the "
                "owner to fix it: write %s/BLOCKED.md and stop." % (work, work)]
    if not os.path.isfile(w("DONE.md")):
        return ["There is no %s/DONE.md yet. Keep working. When you would show this to the owner, write it: one line per "
                "statement bullet, '- true: <the bullet, copied> | evidence: `path` `path`', naming saved evidence files."
                % work]
    rows, problems = {}, []
    for line in HIDDEN.sub("", read(w("DONE.md"))).splitlines():
        m = VERDICT.match(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        text, ev = m.group(2), ""

# Verdict: RM_ReefbackJuv size and RM_Miasma placement

**Size: KEEP the supported sizes (6.4 / 16).**
**Miasma placement: KEEP drawing it.**

Both verdicts are conclusions about the source model, not running-game proof. They are delegated design judgment, not owner approval.

## 1. Size: KEEP

**The item's premise is a base-size conflation.** "Body size 32 … tier 3 by size" reads `baseBodySize`. The `Inherit="False"` override gives the young race only two stages: AnimalBaby (×0.2 → 6.4, T1) and AnimalJuvenile (×0.5 → 16, T2). `Pawn.BodySize` multiplies the stage factor by the base size, and no stage has factor 1, so no living young reefback reaches 32 or T3. The negative controls show the override replaces the stage list rather than appending to it. The measurement refutes the premise.

**The supported sizes match the lineage.** The adult RM_Reefback's own baby and juvenile stages are also 6.4 and 16. Shrinking the young race would make a wild calf smaller than a born calf of the same species. The def's own description supports a large calf: "hatchling-sized by comparison only."

**Shrinking would not fix the real tension.** The Miasma sheet says juveniles are "small and almost charming and cheap to hunt." A 16-size young reefback is not cheap, but body size is not what makes it dangerous. Its inherited combat profile is:
- tail sweep 480 × 0.75 ≈ 360 blunt damage;
- health scale 20 × 0.6 = 12;
- manhunter-on-damage chance 0.2;
- wild groups of 2–3.

Those come from `tools`, `baseHealthScale` and the manhunter fields, which this item does not cover. Lowering the size would move the tier while leaving the "cheap to hunt" contradiction intact.

**The mother-size mismatch is a separate issue.** RM_WardenMother at 8 is smaller than her lineage's juvenile at 16. That tension is real. It sits in the mother's def, whose own comment chose 8 relative to the adult reefback. It is not grounds to resize the calf here, and touching the mother is out of scope.

The "no second giant" ⛔ is the strongest argument against KEEP. A 16-size T2 animal in Miasma groups is arguably giant-class. I read that clause as covering an independent giant species diluting the warden's lane, not her lineage's young. That reading is my judgment, not a ruling. If the owner disagrees, the remedy is a stat or tier decision about the young, not an eviction.

## 2. Miasma placement: KEEP

- **There is an in-game reason for two biomes.** The nursery lifecycle (R11, the_miasma §4, the_grey_deep "bred at the Miasma's crèches") says the young live in the Miasma and the adults in the Grey Sea. Each def still belongs to exactly one biome: RM_ReefbackJuv to Miasma, RM_Reefback to Grey Sea.
- **Removal would be an eviction**, against "Let's stop evictions right now." It would also orphan its other wiring: the `strandedSpawnList` entry and the acoustic payload patch.
- **The roster JSON gap is documentation drift.** The older Miasma nursery list doesn't name RM_ReefbackJuv. That is grounds to update the record later, not to remove the animal.
- **The commonality is plausible.** 0.15 against sibling weights of 0.25–0.4 is a relative draw weight and fits a rarer, heavier nursery member.

## 3. Realistic cases the offline measurement missed

1. **The adult-tier check misclassifies the young race as T3.** `AdultTier` and `DefQualifies` start `maxFactor` at 1f, so RM_ReefbackJuv reports T3 even though no stage exceeds ×0.5. Per its own doc comment, `AdultTier` decides titan-event membership and scavenger-draw exclusion. The young race may therefore sit in the titan passage pool, spawning a "titan" that is really a 16-size T2, and be excluded from scavenger draws. This affects the passage classifier, is independent of size and placement, and needs a classifier-semantics change that is out of scope. It should be filed, not fixed here.
2. **Wild spawns are almost always juveniles.** The young race inherits `lifeExpectancy` 500 and its final stage starts at 0.1 years. Unless a spawn path forces newborns, nearly every wild or stranded young reefback is a 16-size T2, and the 6.4 baby barely appears. The effective size is 16, not the pair of sizes.
3. **The ecosystem budget is skewed.** The young race inherits `ecoSystemWeight` 4.0, so a group of 2–3 consumes about 8–12 weight against density 6.5. That thins the deliberately thick nursery crowd, which commonality alone hides. This is ecology, independent of size.
4. **Stranded calves beside the mother make the mismatch visible.** The mother "sometimes brings stranded young," which would put a 16-size calf next to an 8-size mother. This is a player-visible lineage oddity, but it belongs to the mother and lore lane.
5. **Only default thresholds were measured.** Custom tiers (e.g., T2 above 16) move the calf. Large Pawns rendering at `drawSize` 4.42 for a 16-size pawn was not checked, and art is out of scope.

## 4. Suggested bounded checks (offline)

1. **Titan-pool membership.** From source, enumerate which pools include RM_ReefbackJuv through `AdultTier` or `DefQualifies` (titan passage pool, scavenger draw, Large Pawns rows, wake auto-attach) under default thresholds. If it is in the titan passage pool, file a separate classifier item. No semantics change in this item.
2. **Stage share at spawn.** Resolve the wild and stranded spawn age paths for the young race (age generation with `lifeExpectancy` 500, final `minAge` 0.1) and report the expected baby/juvenile share. Optionally add its ecosystem-weight share against the Miasma siblings.

## 5. Scope boundary

- **Concluded from source:** living-pawn sizes and tiers, list replacement, biome wiring, and that no repository patch alters these values.
- **Not shown:** spawn frequency, actual stage mix, passage events, combat, pathing, rendering, or any running-game behaviour. Nothing here is deployment, art or first-touch acceptance.
- **Independent issues, not part of this size/placement decision:** the `AdultTier` 1f floor, the inherited combat profile versus "cheap to hunt," the ecosystem weight, and the mother/calf size ratio.

Opus acknowledged the “no second giant” concern and judged this lineage’s young consistent with the nursery, rather than an unrelated replacement giant. That is delegated judgment within existing constraints, not a new interpretation attributed to the owner. External mods/settings remain outside this source model.

Key SHA-256 provenance (full manifest in `evidence/raw/measure/inputs.json`):

- Reefback source `{h('"'src/RimMandrake/TerminalBiomes/Defs/ThingDefs_Races/RM_SeaBeasts_Invented.xml')}"'`.

# Independent Codex judgment — REEFBACK_CALF_MEASURE_TITAN_ON_LAND

2026-11-11. Fresh examination of the permitted statement, evidence and source; I did not build this work. **Accept the offline measurement and the decision to KEEP the supported sizes and KEEP the Miasma row.** This is not a finding that the nursery's gameplay balance is correct. The classifier discrepancy and inherited combat concern remain explicitly unresolved below.

Only this file was written. Each shell sourced the specified testcentre environment and exported `RIMFLOW_SEAT`, `AGENT_SEAT` and `RIMFLOW_BRIDGE_SEAT` as `CODEX_STEVEDESKTOP_HUGETHINGS`, with all three names in `WSLENV`. No game, bridge, deployment, build, DLL execution, network, ledger, commit or other clone was used. No builder decision document, builder verdict or previous judgment was consulted.

## Exact frozen bullets

1. **TRUE, for offline source measurement:** “Measure the young reefback's effective body sizes and HugeThings tiers at every supported life stage, distinguishing the inherited base size from a living pawn's size and the passage classifier; compare the adult reefback with exact source provenance.”

   The independently calculated stage table below agrees with `evidence/raw/measure/measurement.json`, but the agreement was checked against actual XML and the retained engine instruction text rather than accepted from its labels. The child replaces both inherited lists; its living size never reaches the inherited base size under these supported stages. `AdultTier` is a distinct calculation and returns T3. Sources: [race and kind definitions](../../src/RimMandrake/TerminalBiomes/Defs/ThingDefs_Races/RM_SeaBeasts_Invented.xml), [Core snapshot](evidence/raw/measure/snapshots/Core-LifeStages.xml), [engine instructions](evidence/raw/measure/snapshots/engine-selected.il.txt), [tier consumer](../../src/RimMandrake/HugeThings/Source/Titanic/Tiering/TitanicTierUtility.cs), and [raw measurements](evidence/raw/measure/measurement.json).

2. **TRUE, as the bounded design decision recorded here:** “Decide whether the calf needs smaller sizes and whether Miasma should keep drawing it, using the established nursery lifecycle, current roster and independent delegated design judgment; apply any warranted correction without inventing an owner ruling or evicting roster residents.”

   **KEEP sizes 6.4/16; KEEP `RM_Miasma/wildAnimals/RM_ReefbackJuv` at 0.15.** The false adult-size premise does not warrant a resize. The nursery's own lineage has these same baby/juvenile sizes; removing an established resident contradicts both the lifecycle and stopped evictions. The independent delegated response recommends both KEEP decisions, with concerns considered below. This is delegated judgment, not owner approval. No size or roster correction is warranted by the measured premise, and none was made by this judge. Sources: [item premise](evidence/item-before.txt), [independent design prompt](evidence/design_prompt.txt), [independent design response, `result`](evidence/design_raw.json), [Miasma source](../../src/RimMandrake/Miasma/Defs/BiomeDefs/RM_Miasma.xml), [nursery specification](../../design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/the_miasma.md), and [stopped-eviction rule](../../CLAUDE.md).

3. **TRUE, at the explicitly offline scope:** “Retain reproducible offline evidence and a fresh independent Codex judgment for the complete decision; report its exact limits and make no live, deployment, flight, art-appearance or first-touch acceptance claim.”

   The raw directory retains source selections, Core and consumer snapshots, input hashes, IL-reading process source, process receipts, numeric measurements and mutation fixtures. The measurement implementation is available as [Python source](../../src/RimMandrake/HugeThings/northstar/measure_reefback_calf.py). This file provides the fresh judgment. I independently checked 21 eligible input hashes from [the manifest](evidence/raw/measure/inputs.json), with zero mismatches, and confirmed the Core snapshots match the installed Core XML and the engine-text snapshot matches `evidence/raw/engine.stdout.txt`. This did not re-disassemble or authenticate the installed engine binary. The [process receipt](evidence/raw/engine.receipt.json) describes reflection-only metadata inspection, and [the retained reader](evidence/raw/measure/snapshots/read_engine.ps1) uses `ReflectionOnlyLoadFrom` and decodes IL. These are offline provenance, never runtime proof. Missing runtime measurement is not a defect of this task.

## Re-derived sizes and inheritance

`RM_SeaBeasts_Invented.xml:1314` defines the named adult parent, inheriting `AnimalThingBase`; `:1355` supplies `baseBodySize=32`; `:1364` supplies three stages. The young ThingDef at `:1840` inherits that named parent and replaces `race/lifeStageAges` with `Inherit="False"` at `:1845`. Its PawnKindDef inherits `RM_Reefback_Kind` and independently replaces `lifeStages` at `:1863`. Both resulting child lists have exactly two entries. The Core `AnimalThingBase` and `AnimalKindBase` ancestry is retained in [the Core base snapshot](evidence/raw/measure/snapshots/Core-Races_Animal_Base.xml).

Core `LifeStages.xml` defines `AnimalBaby.bodySizeFactor=0.2` and `AnimalJuvenile.bodySizeFactor=0.5`. `AnimalAdult` omits the field; the retained `LifeStageDef::.ctor` instructions set it to 1 (`engine-selected.il.txt:45–47`). `Pawn::get_BodySize` loads the current stage factor and `RaceProps.baseBodySize`, multiplies them and returns (`:287–296`). No draw-size value enters this multiplication.

| Race | Supported stage | XML minAge, years | Factor | Effective BodySize | Default GetTier |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| RM_ReefbackJuv | AnimalBaby | 0 | 0.2 | 6.4 | T1 |
| RM_ReefbackJuv | AnimalJuvenile | 0.1 | 0.5 | 16 | T2 |
| RM_Reefback | AnimalBaby | 0 | 0.2 | 6.4 | T1 |
| RM_Reefback | AnimalJuvenile | 0.2 | 0.5 | 16 | T2 |
| RM_Reefback | AnimalAdult | 0.6 | 1 | 32 | T3 |

The float32 baby result is `6.400000095367432`; 16 and 32 are exact. I calculated these with an independent, in-memory selected-shape inheritance resolver and float32 multiplication, then compared every stage/factor result with the raw numeric evidence. I also independently obtained the warden mother's sizes 1.6/4/8/8, tiers None/T1/T2/T2, at XML stage ages 0/0.15/0.4/38 from [her source](../../src/RimMandrake/Miasma/Defs/ThingDefs_Races/RM_WardenMother.xml). That exposes a real design tension: a juvenile reefback at 16 exceeds the elder mother's size 8. It does not establish a different authorized calf size.

These minAge values are XML provenance, not exact observed transition times. The engine text calculates clamped growth against the final stage age, then selects stages backwards with `1E-06` tolerance (`engine-selected.il.txt:318–422`). Aging a young-race pawn does not append an adult entry or convert its race. In-memory checks at model ages 0, 0.099, 0.1, 1, 500 and 1000 selected only the two supported child sizes. No implemented migration to the adult species was demonstrated.

The original assertion in `item-before.txt` is therefore **FALSE as an effective pawn-size/T3 assertion**. Its base-size 32 and Miasma weight 0.15 components are **TRUE**. Its T3 component survives only for the separate def-level classifier.

## Tier consumers and patch coverage

The shipped [tier XML](../../src/RimMandrake/HugeThings/Defs/TitanicTierDefs/RM_TitanicTierDef.xml) sets inclusive floors 4/8/20. `TitanicTierUtility.GetTier` reads `pawn.BodySize` (`:112–126`); [the kernel](../../src/RimMandrake/HugeThings/Source/Kernel/RM_TitanicKernel.cs) applies the ladder and force overrides. No selected race inherits a Titanic force extension. Custom thresholds and external mods are outside the numeric result.

`AdultTier` starts `maxFactor=1f` and only raises it (`TitanicTierUtility.cs:94–105`). Thus the child reports `TierFor(32*1)=T3` although its maximum supported living tier is T2. `DefQualifies` uses the same conservative floor (`:78–91`); at defaults it attaches the wake comp. Its T1 qualification is correct for this calf even using its actual maximum size. [LargePawnsBridge](../../src/RimMandrake/HugeThings/Source/Titanic/Footprint/LargePawnsBridge.cs):168–195 adds per-race rows only for explicit force extensions; it adds no calf-specific override here. This proves source wiring, not actual rendering or footprint behavior.

I independently scanned all 497 repository XML files containing `<xpath>` (52,876 selectors, no parse errors), including lanes omitted from the retained 474-file [patch audit](evidence/raw/measure/patch-audit.json). I inspected broad selectors, root additions, selected names, ancestry, life stages, biome rows and tier fields. No repository patch changes the selected base size, stage factors, stage list replacement, default thresholds or calf commonality. Relevant other effects are:

- [FaunaNorm_Law5_Tolerance.xml](../../src/RimUtinni/UtinniPatches/Patches/FaunaNorm_Law5_Tolerance.xml):3221–3244 raises the calf's upper temperature tolerance to at least 73.3 when active.
- [FaunaNorm_Law6_Products.xml](../../src/RimUtinni/UtinniPatches/Patches/FaunaNorm_Law6_Products.xml):1560–1604 supplies MeatAmount 4480 to adult and calf. Its base-size comments are not stage-size measurements. `Doctrine/Patches/MegafaunaYield.xml` targets the distinct `RSW_Reefback`, not this RM race.
- [WildAnimals_Miasma.xml](../../src/RimUtinni/UtinniPatches/Patches/WildAnimals_Miasma.xml) adds other residents without removing or replacing this calf row. Acoustic payload patches add references to calf/adult; Grey Sea seabed wiring adds extensions. Ancestor-wide surgery patches affect recipes. None changes the measured fields.
- The only located repository `Pawn.BodySize` getter patch is [Dhoggur swell](../../src/RimMandrake/TheForge/Source/RM_ForgeDhoggurSwell.cs):297–305, conditional on its registry. The registry is populated by the Dhoggur comp, attached by `TheForge/Defs/ThingDefs_Races/RM_Dhoggur.xml:115`; it is absent from the selected reefback ancestry. The located C# base-size reassignment in `Pyrelands/Source/RM_PyrelandsGiants.cs:165–168` belongs to the furnace beast.

This is a repository source audit, not an execution of RimWorld's full patch loader or inspection of a live mod list.

## Placement, aliases and delegated reasoning

The [Miasma sheet](../../design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/the_miasma.md):97–127 explicitly puts the Grey Sea lineage's young in nursery shallows and its elders at crèches. [The Grey Deep sheet](../../design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/the_grey_deep.md):101 and :120–123 identifies the crusted giant lineage, bred at those crèches, and its `RM_Reefback` implementation. There is no `the_grey_sea.md` at the supplied path; the allowed related Grey Deep source establishes that mapping.

The current [Miasma roster JSON](../../design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/rosters/the_miasma.json) has R11 nursery rows and a warden lifecycle entry, but no named `RM_ReefbackJuv` row. The [Grey Sea roster JSON](../../design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/rosters/the_grey_sea.json), `fauna[0]`, retains historical `RSW_Reefback` wording and explicitly says the built adult ships as `RM_Reefback` at 0.005. Do not merge their identities: `RM_SeaBeasts_Invented.xml:19–34` and `SWBestiary/Defs/SeaBeasts/ThingDefs_Races/SeaBeasts_Colossi.xml:31,98` establish separate RM and RSW pairs. The child's actual parent is the RM pair. The roster's historical statistics do not override actual source.

The implemented calf is already resident at Miasma weight 0.15 (`RM_Miasma.xml:247`), in its stranded list (`:159`), the [crèche young list](../../src/RimMandrake/Miasma/Defs/MapGeneration/RM_Miasma_CrecheScatterer.xml):98, and its [acoustic payload](../../src/RimMandrake/Miasma/Patches/RM_AcousticPayload_Miasma.xml):42. The adult is on [RM_GreySea.xml](../../src/RimMandrake/TerminalBiomes/Defs/BiomeDefs/RM_GreySea.xml):81 at 0.005. The nursery is an established in-game reason under `CLAUDE.md:72–76`; the stopped-eviction instruction independently weighs against removal. Missing roster documentation is not an eviction instruction.

The independent design response's KEEP reasoning is persuasive on the false size premise, lineage and resident retention. Its interpretation of “no second giant” is reasonable for the same nursery lineage, but remains delegated interpretation: the mother's giant role is not overwritten by this judgment. A 16-size animal is still very large. Weight 0.15 is a relative selection weight, not a measured encounter frequency. I do not adopt the response's comparison of group ecosystem weight 8–12 directly with animalDensity 6.5 as a quantitative population conclusion; those are different quantities and the full budget calculation was not measured.

## Consequences and unresolved gameplay concerns

The design response's classifier concern is real as a numeric discrepancy, but its consequences require precision. [TitanPassage.cs](../../src/RimMandrake/HugeThings/Source/Titanic/Events/TitanPassage.cs):55–73 uses `AdultTier`, home/commonality, water classification, season and passage-list gates. The calf's source home is land-classified Miasma; the adult's is water-classified Grey Sea. This permits the calf on a suitable Miasma map when other gates allow, without admitting the adult there. Correcting the calf's classifier from T3 to its supported maximum T2 would still pass the event's T2 minimum.

There is a concrete difference in spacing: `RM_TitanicKernel.cs:212–217` rejects a T3-classified candidate when a live T3 stands on the map, whereas a T2 candidate would remain eligible. `TitanPassage.cs:118–120` counts existing T3s using current `GetTier`. Thus the calf can be blocked as a T3 candidate without ever counting as a living T3 after arrival. This deserves a classifier-semantics review; it cannot be dismissed as merely a display label or fixed by pretending the calf has BodySize 32. Conversely, source comments explicitly intend calf-lineage eligibility and conservative def qualification, so the discrepancy alone does not establish that a lineage-based event classifier is unintended. No classifier correction or bug-free gameplay certification is included here.

The suggested scavenger consequence is overstated for this animal: [CorpseSiteVisitors.cs](../../src/RimMandrake/HugeThings/Source/Titanic/CorpseSite/CorpseSiteVisitors.cs):25–28 requires a predator with AdultTier None. This calf is non-predatory and would fail even if classified T2. Its exclusion is not evidence of a new scavenger regression.

The inherited combat concern remains substantial: the calf retains tail-sweep power 480, bulk power 120, health scale 20 and manhunter-on-damage chance 0.2 (`RM_SeaBeasts_Invented.xml:1328–1362`). Core stage melee factors are 0.5/0.75, leaving nominal tail-sweep products 240/360 before other combat mechanics. This sits poorly with the nursery sheet's “cheap to hunt.” Actual hits and combat outcomes were not tested. **This is an unresolved balance/specification concern, not accepted gameplay and not silently waived by KEEP.** Changing body size alone would not correct inherited tools or health. The mother's size inversion likewise remains visible rather than being claimed resolved.

The design response's spawn-age follow-up can be narrowed offline. The wild spawn IL calls ordinary `GeneratePawn` (`engine-selected.il.txt:213–218`); stranding (`RM_MapComponent_StrandingPools.cs:263–265`) and crèche young generation (`RM_SetPieceElement_AnchoredPawn.cs:124–130`) do not force a newborn age. With no selected age-generation curve and life expectancy 500, the retained default curve spans normalized ages 0.05–1.25 (`engine-selected.il.txt:1135–1184`), yielding proposal ages 25–625 years, already beyond the child's last stage. Under that normal generation branch, successful proposals are juveniles at size 16. This is not an observed stage distribution, and special newborn/fixed-age requests are separate branches. Nursery travel, maturation into another species and real encounter frequency remain unproved.

## Negative controls and limits

I reproduced [the negative fixtures](evidence/raw/measure/negative-controls.json) independently in memory. Removing the race replacement marker produces `[Baby, Juvenile, Adult, Baby, Juvenile]`; removing the kind marker produces five graphics entries. The same-list parent/child fixture produces four entries without replacement versus two with it. These reject append semantics and a vacuous same-list test. They do **not** prove the malformed list makes a T3 pawn: reverse selection can shadow the inherited adult. The base-only oracle's size 32/T3 disagrees with both correctly resolved child stages, independently rejecting the item's conflation.

The evidence establishes offline selected-source arithmetic, source consumer behavior and a reasoned KEEP/KEEP decision. It does not establish running-game patch order, saved settings, external mods, population balance, combat balance, pathing, art appearance, deployment, flight, first-touch acceptance or completed lifecycle transport. The remaining gameplay concerns are retained above for substantive follow-up; this judgment neither edits another lane nor claims those concerns fixed.
